Area.evidence_source: [page/3/Text/9] Farmers felt that they were failing in their relationships and it seemed to be an important proximal factor contributing to suicide. This was interrelated with cultural norms of masculinity and with the family, land and the commodity. Norms associated with subsequent feelings of failure included: family-of-origin expectation of the farm staying in the family name (succession farming); sons inheriting the family farm; keeping up with other farmers in the district (eg, having enough stock during drought); land autonomy; and antiauthoritarian attitudes to regulatory procedures.
